text.p: The Sierra Club and two other environmental groups on Saturday endorsed President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore for re-election at a rally attended by Gore.
"The President used his veto pen to reject Congress' attack on basic clean air, water and lands protections," Sierra Club president Adam Werbach said at the rally in a Washington, D.C., park.

Werbach said Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole "spent 27 years in the Senate pandering to America's polluters and plunderers. Dole and (vice presidential candidate Jack) Kemp are the most anti-environment ticket nominated for president since the first Earth Day."
The Sierra Club listed its membership at 600,000 nationwide. Also presenting their endorsements to Clinton/Gore were Clean Water Action and the League of Conservation Voters.

In accepting the endorsements, Gore said he and Clinton were committed to protecting the environment and "will not let Bob Dole, (House Speaker) Newt Gingrich and extreme anti-environmentalists in Congress destroy 25 years of progress on safe water, clearn air or toxic waste standards."
